issues.legal_issue: Requirements to record and account for forest wood in sawmills and sawpits do not violate the rights to equality or to carry on a trade merely because they impose recordkeeping burdens or discrepancies arise in individual cases.
material_facts: The scheme required persons controlling sawmills and sawpits to record wood received, sawn and disposed of, and to submit periodic returns.
Wood purchased at government depots was identified and its details were provided to purchasers, including through possession and transit documents.

The appellants argued that sawing caused wastage that made exact accounting impracticable, burdened their business and could lead to confiscation; they also alleged an instance of confiscation over a minor discrepancy.

The court found that the records and forms enabled officials to verify the wood's lawful source and track its receipt and disposal, and that the prescribed process left no gap in identifying the wood.
issues.conclusion: The accounting requirements were not unconstitutional under Articles 14 or 19(1)(g) on the grounds advanced. A shortfall or discrepancy, or an allegedly arbitrary enforcement action, does not by itself invalidate the scheme; an individual enforcement action must be assessed on its own facts.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Articles 14 and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution. It considered sections 7, 8 and 9 of the Madhya Pradesh Kashtha Chiran (Viniyaman) Adhiniyam, 1984, concerning inspection, returns and accounting for wood, and section 13 concerning penalties; it also considered rules 6(1)–(3) and 8 of the M.P. Transit (Forest Produce) Rules, 1961, concerning the prescribed records and returns. Recordkeeping requirements serving the purpose of verifying lawful possession and preventing illicit sourcing are not unconstitutional merely because compliance is burdensome or discrepancies may occur. Enforcement in an individual case depends on its facts. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_forest_wood_: A person challenges the constitutionality of requirements for recording and accounting for forest wood held or processed at a sawmill or sawpit.
predicates.wood_details_given_to_purchasers: The authorities provide purchasers with details identifying the wood and documents recording its delivery or transport.
predicates.records_track_receipt_and_disposal: Persons controlling the sawmill or sawpit must record wood received, processed and disposed of and provide returns of those records.
predicates.accounting_requirements_serve_lawful_sou: The records enable officials to check whether the wood came from a lawful source and was properly accounted for.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a forest-wood accounting scheme, the wood details are supplied to purchasers, the records track receipt and disposal, and the requirements enable verification of lawful sourcing, the scheme is not unconstitutional on those grounds.
